issues.detail: Covers the main setup paths but has almost no troubleshooting or error scenarios (e.g., permission denied, token creator propagation delay, ADC quota project errors, expired credentials) beyond a single note on OAuth access scopes.
The two Examples are prose descriptions of scenarios with no concrete commands, inputs, or outputs, so they are less realistic demonstrations than the code blocks in Instructions.

scenarios.name: local-dev-bigquery-impersonation
scenarios.rationale: Both cover impersonation with Token Creator, ADC login with --impersonate-service-account, set-quota-project, and no keys; B also explicitly runs `gcloud config set project`, which the rubric names, while A sets the project only through an env var and the quota-project command, so B is slightly more complete.

scenarios.name: gke-migrate-off-json-key-secret
scenarios.rationale: Both responses cover the rubric's core: workload-pool and GKE_METADATA, a direct principal:// grant, redeploying without the Secret mount, deleting the Secret and key, and the GSA fallback. B edges ahead because it checks the cluster's current state first, scopes the grant to the bucket, adds verification steps, and disables the key before deleting it; A grants at project level and does not verify the cluster state first.

scenarios.name: private-cloud-run-service-to-service
scenarios.rationale: Both cover the run.invoker binding, fetch_id_token with the service URL as audience, and the Bearer header, and neither suggests keys or shared secrets; A adds ingress and AuthorizedSession detail, while B explicitly says no JSON key, API key or shared secret is needed but is a bit thinner.
